explanation: At standard temperature and pressure (STP: 0 C = 273.15 K and 1 atm), one mole of ANY ideal gas occupies the same molar volume, 22.4 L/mol, a direct consequence of Avogadro's law that equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules. So the volume of a gas at STP is simply V = n x 22.4 L, a straight line through the origin. In gas stoichiometry you first use the balanced equation's mole ratio to find moles of gas, then multiply by 22.4 L/mol for the volume at STP. On the AP exam, remember 22.4 L/mol applies only at STP — away from STP you must use PV = nRT instead.
bullets: V vs n is a straight line through the origin with slope 22.4 L/mol.
Holds for any ideal gas at STP (0 C, 1 atm) — Avogadro's law.
The shaded box height = computed volume V for the chosen moles n.
Each mole = 6.022 x 10^23 molecules (shown in the live readout).
